second_speaker_utterance_with_correspond: Preserving Britain's national identity demands embracing humanitarian immigration, since historical waves like the Windrush generation have enriched our multicultural society and decreased inequality, proving that openness strengthens rather than fragments our cohesion.

Prioritising only skilled workers ignores how refugees and diverse migrants fill essential roles in healthcare and care sectors, preventing shortages that would actually overwhelm the NHS and harm British citizens, as NHS reports confirm.

Strict controls don't prevent illegal crossings; they drive desperate refugees into the hands of criminal smugglers, increasing crime and insecurity, whereas loosening through expanded legal humanitarian pathways reduces irregular migration and enhances national security as UNHCR reports clearly demonstrate.
Dismantling smuggling networks requires providing safe, legal routes for vulnerable migrants rather than deterring them with harsh barriers that only exacerbate the dangers and chaos at our borders.

We shouldn't risk overwhelming the NHS by excluding humanitarian migrants because ONS data shows all migrants, including refugees, contribute £4.3 billion more in taxes than they receive in benefits, directly funding and bolstering the NHS for everyone without any net drain.
